chunks: Jamil ibn Salih narrated from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who had three virgin daughters. He married one of them to a man, but did not specify to the husband nor to the witnesses which one he had married off. The husband had fixed a dowry for her. Then when the time came for him to consummate the marriage with her, and the husband was informed that she was the eldest, the husband said to her father: I only married from you the youngest of your daughters.

So Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "If the husband had seen all of them, and none of them had been specifically named to him, then in that matter the father's word is accepted. But it is upon the father, in what is between him and Allah عزّ وجلّ, to hand over to the husband the girl whom he had intended to marry to him at the time of the marriage contract. But if the husband had not seen all of them, and none of them had been specifically named to him at the time of the marriage contract, then the marriage is invalid."

key_terms.أَبْكَارٍ: virgin daughters who had not previously married
key_terms.الْأَبِ: the father, whose statement is considered in this dispute
key_terms.صَدَاقًا: the dowry agreed upon for the marriage
key_terms.عُقْدَةِ النِّكَاحِ: the formal binding of the marriage contract
key_terms.نَوَى: intended internally at the time of the contract

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father marries off one of several daughters without specifying which one in the marriage contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on a marriage contract in which the bride was not specifically identified. If the husband had seen all the daughters, the father's statement is treated as authoritative, though the father remains accountable before Allah عزّ وجلّ to deliver the one he truly intended at the time of the contract. If the husband had not seen all of them and no daughter was specified, the nikah is invalid.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4468 - Jamil ibn Salih narrated from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who had three unmarried daughters.
He married one of them to a man but did not specify which daughter to the husband or the witnesses. The husband had already agreed upon a dowry for her.
When the time came for the husband to consummate the marriage, he was informed that the bride was the eldest daughter. However, the husband said to the father, "I only intended to marry your youngest daughter."

Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) replied: "If the husband had seen all the daughters and had not specified one of them, then the decision is based on the father's word. However, the father must, before Allah (swt) (Glorified and Exalted), give the husband the daughter he intended to marry off at the time of the marriage contract.
But if the husband had not seen all the daughters and no specific one was identified during the marriage contract, then the marriage is invalid."
